evaluation_method: Actual reference-plus-six-time-frame mosaics for correct music, swapped music and zero music on the same three people, plus full-frame RGB difference and fixed-context val200 token audit. Not continuous audio listening or user preference feedback.

visual_cases.staircase: Original music and swapped music repeat palm/hand gestures and backward leg lifts, with limited timing/end variations. Zero music still produces this action family. All use white/navy sportswear and a small bag instead of the reference pale yellow top/grey trousers.
visual_cases.red_shirt: Hand-near-face, head-side arm movements and forward hand gestures remain similar across original/swapped/zero music. Reference red clothing is broadly retained. Legs cropped, no footwork accuracy claim.
visual_cases.store: Mostly low-amplitude single-arm, torso and weight changes. Original/swapped/zero retain related motifs; cannot establish complete paired MotionScript sequence or musical correctness.

conclusion: Training and deployment now execute the same complete raw-token mapping. This is necessary but insufficient: direct per-word-position regression mostly learns shared token distribution rather than demonstrated musical control. Correct music does not materially improve token fit over wrong music and is worse than a train-only positional mean. Generated videos preserve similar motifs with music replaced or zeroed; reference outfit drift remains. No established useful music-driven dance increment from this first recipe.
next_boundary: Do not blindly expand data or claim omitted adapter was the only problem. Teacher representations/sequence supervision and contrastive musical dependency need redesign; any new generator-level loss requires separate authorization. Identity text and first-frame lock remain postponed.
